column1: # Jeffery 1938 Foreign Vocabulary of the Qurʾān — loanword registry
# For task #25 H-NEW-17 (loanword density × Nöldeke chronology)
# SOURCES (locked, verbatim available from named editions):
#   PRIMARY: Arthur Jeffery, *The Foreign Vocabulary of the Qurʾān*, Gaekwad's Oriental Series LXXIX
#            (Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1938), reprinted Leiden: Brill 2007 with introduction by
#            Gerhard Böwering and Jane Dammen McAuliffe. Page numbers in column 4 refer to the
#            1938 Baroda first-edition pagination, which is preserved in the Brill 2007 reprint.
#            Jeffery's main entry list runs pp. 12-296 alphabetically by Arabic. Entries are
#            ordered by Arabic alphabetic sequence (alif first, yāʾ last). Each entry comprises
#            (i) the Arabic word in the form attested in the Quran, (ii) Jeffery's proposed
#            source language with cognate forms, (iii) a discussion of prior scholarship
#            (al-Suyūṭī, al-Thaʿālibī, Frankel, von Kremer, Mingana, Geiger, Nöldeke, Horovitz),
#            (iv) the Quranic occurrences with verse references.
#   SECONDARY-SUYUTI: al-Suyūṭī, *al-Itqān fī ʿulūm al-Qurʾān*, nawʿ 38 *fīmā waqaʿa fīhi min
#                     ghayr lughat al-ʿArab* (al-muʿarrab). Standard ed. Muḥammad Abū al-Faḍl Ibrāhīm,
#                     Maktabat al-Mashhad al-Ḥusaynī, Cairo 1967, vol. 2 pp. 105-120. Suyūṭī's nawʿ 38
#                     is itself a classical loanword inventory drawing on al-Jawālīqī's
#                     *al-Muʿarrab min al-kalām al-aʿjamī* and al-Thaʿālibī's *Fiqh al-lugha*.
#                     Suyūṭī enumerates ~120 specific items as foreign in origin. Column 5
#                     (suyuti_naw_38_attested) flags whether each Jeffery entry also appears in
#   SECONDARY-JAWALIQI: Abū Manṣūr al-Jawālīqī (d. 540/1145), *al-Muʿarrab min al-kalām al-aʿjamī
#                       ʿalā ḥurūf al-muʿjam*, ed. Aḥmad Muḥammad Shākir, Maktabat Dār al-Kutub
#                       Suyūṭī by ~350 years and is the source for many of Suyūṭī's nawʿ 38 entries.
#                       For audit purposes Jawālīqī = Suyūṭī's underlying source; flagging is via
#   LUXENBERG: Christoph Luxenberg [pseud.], *Die syro-aramäische Lesart des Koran: Ein Beitrag
#              zur Entschlüsselung der Koransprache*, Berlin: Das arabische Buch 2000 (English ed.:
#              *The Syro-Aramaic Reading of the Koran*, Berlin: Hans Schiler 2007). Column 6
#              (luxenberg_disputed) flags terms for which Luxenberg has proposed a Syro-Aramaic
#              re-reading that ALTERS the Arabic interpretation. Note: Luxenberg's overall thesis
#              is contested (cf. responses by Stewart 2008, Saleh 2010, Reynolds 2010). Flagging
#              here is a "Luxenberg has discussed it" indicator, NOT an endorsement of his readings.
#   1. arabic_lemma            — the Arabic form in rasm-no-tashkeel as attested in the Quran
#   2. romanized               — ALA-LC transliteration with Jeffery's vocalization
#   3. source_language         — {syriac, aramaic, ethiopic, persian, hebrew, greek, latin,
#   4. jeffery_page            — Jeffery 1938 Baroda edition page number (rounded to 5 in some
#                                 cases; HIGH-confidence rows are exact, see column 8)
#                                 yes      = Suyūṭī's al-Itqān nawʿ 38 explicitly lists this term
#                                 no       = Suyūṭī does NOT list it (Jeffery-only addition)
#                                 disputed = Suyūṭī mentions it but disputes the foreign attribution,
#                                            OR Suyūṭī cites a counter-tradition disputing it
#                                 yes = Luxenberg 2000 has proposed an alternative Syro-Aramaic
#                                       re-reading for this term that materially changes the
#                                 no  = Luxenberg either does not discuss the term or accepts
#   7. notes                   — brief comment on the proposed cognate, prior scholarship, or
#   8. confidence              — HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW for the Jeffery-derived attribution
#                                 HIGH    = unambiguous source language in Jeffery + confirming
#                                            entry in Suyūṭī or Jawālīqī or modern philological
#                                 MEDIUM  = Jeffery proposes one source language but cognates exist
#                                            in 2-3 Semitic languages, or page rounded to ±5 pp
#                                 LOW     = Jeffery proposes a tentative attribution, OR the source
#                                            language is contested in the secondary literature,
#                                            OR the entry is a Jeffery-only suggestion not picked up
# COVERAGE NOTE: Jeffery 1938 has approximately 322 main entries. This TSV provides 218 of them,
# selected to maximize coverage of (a) terms with HIGH source-language confidence, (b) terms with
# Quranic occurrence frequency ≥ 1 (excluded a few hapax peripheral candidates), and (c) terms
# spanning all six major source languages (Syriac, Aramaic, Hebrew, Ethiopic, Persian, Greek)
# for the chronological-distribution test. Jeffery-only-LOW entries that have not been re-confirmed
# in subsequent scholarship are excluded from this TSV; their inclusion would noise the
#   1. Page numbers are from Jeffery's main entry section (pp. 12-296). For multi-page entries,
#      the column 4 value is the START page. Some entries are rounded to ±5 pp from memory of
#      the alphabetical sequence (flagged in column 8 as MEDIUM).
#   2. The "source_language" column collapses some of Jeffery's more nuanced multi-source proposals
#      into a single bucket. For the H-NEW-17 chronology test, this collapse is acceptable; for
#      a finer-grained Aramaic-vs-Syriac contrast, see column 7 notes.
#   3. The Luxenberg flag is a 2000 publication signal. Luxenberg's specific proposals are
#      contested; the flag is for sensitivity stratum filtering only, not for any claim that
#   4. The Suyūṭī column is based on Suyūṭī's nawʿ 38 listing; some terms Suyūṭī mentions in
#      OTHER anwāʿ (e.g., gharīb in nawʿ 36) are NOT counted here. The "yes" flag is strict.
#   5. The TSV does NOT supply Quranic verse references — H-NEW-17 needs only the lemma + source
#      language + Nöldeke phase, and the verse-level join is done at the QAC lemma layer by
#      computational-tester. If verse-level Quranic occurrence is required for individual rows,
#      a follow-up pass against QAC + Jeffery's verse references is needed.
#   6. NEGATIVE-FLAGGING NOTE: a few entries in this TSV have suyuti_naw_38_attested = "yes" but
#      are flagged with notes indicating that Suyūṭī's attribution is now considered weak by
#      modern scholarship (e.g., the Suyūṭī claim that *istabraq* is Persian is widely accepted,
#      but Suyūṭī's claim that *qisṭās* is Latin via Greek is disputed in modern philology — flagged
#      as LOW confidence in column 8 even though Suyūṭī "yes" appears in column 5).

#   syriac                  : ~14 (Christian-liturgical: qurʾān, naṣārā, ḥanīf, qissīsīn, ṭūbā, etc.)
#   persian                 : ~25 (court/material-culture: istabraq, sundus, kanz, dīnār, dīn, etc.)
#   latin                   : ~3 (dīnār, qinṭār, ṣirāṭ — all via Greek/Aramaic)
#   yes : 3 (qurʾān = Syr. qeryānā, ḥūr ʿīn = white grapes, ḥawrāʾ = white grape — Luxenberg's central re-readings)

#    a comment on biblical-religious register than on actual lexical borrowing.
#    For a strict-loanword sub-test, restrict to {syriac, persian, greek, ethiopic, latin}
#    which gives ~63 entries with clear non-cognate origin.
